title: Quantitative Studies of Cool Flame Transitions at Radiation / Stretch Extinction Using Counterflow Flames

summary.text: This investigation aims to conduct simulations and ground-based experiments with ozone-sensitized counterflow flames, and hypothesizes that oxygen concentration, dilution, pressure, diffusion, and convection affect the cool flame transition.

fuels.text: n-heptane/air mixture and dimethyl ether (DME)/air mixtures in the modeling schemes.

geometry.text: One-dimensional geometry is to be maintained, using counterflow flames.

oxygen.text: Oxygen concentration effects on cool-flame extinction limits were studied with three numerical modeling schemes.

pressure.text: Cool flame regimes and burning limits were simulated at elevated pressure (up to 20 atm).

measurements.text: Objective: obtain quantitative data of extinction limit, flame temperature, and species distribution (intended measurements).

claims.text: The grant aims to conduct new simulations and ground-based experiments using ozone-sensitized counterflow flames.
The investigation hypothesizes that oxygen concentration, dilution, pressure, diffusion, and convection transport processes affect the cool flame transition.

limitations.text: The metadata field for research impacts contains statements phrased as results (for example, a warm flame double reaction zone structure). These were not recorded as reported observations because they appear in an impacts field, not in a document or an observation field.
This draft cites PSI metadata and no PDF text. The packet also includes official table passages whose findings have not been incorporated or reviewed.

modeling_resources.description: Candidate data for modeling: data summary table and workbook linked to the quantitative extinction, temperature and species data that the objectives set out to obtain. No model validation is claimed.

evidence.excerpt: to conduct new simulations and ground-based experiments using ozone-sensitized counterflow flames
The investigation hypothesizes that factors such as oxygen concentration, dilution, pressure, diffusion, and convection transport processes affect the cool flame transition.

(a) spark-assisted flame propagation of a n-heptane/air mixture, (b) one dimensional freely-propagating dimethyl ether (DME) flames using an arc-length continuation method and (c) simulated cool flame regimes and burning limits at elevated pressure (up to 20 atm) using DME/air mixtures
Obtain new, quantitative data of extinction limit, flame temperature, and species distribution
comparative studies of the oxygen concentration effects on the extinction limits of cool flames was conducted using three different numerical modeling schemes
The results showed that the warm flame has a double reaction zone structure
